asked.ask: How long can cooked rice sit out on the counter before it is unsafe?
replies: Sam: Two hours at room temperature is the limit. If it's hot out, over about 32°C (90°F), cut that to one hour. The trouble is a bacterium called Bacillus cereus. Its spores survive cooking, then multiply in warm rice and can make a toxin. Reheating won't destroy that toxin, so rice that sat out too long can still make you sick, even if it smells fine. First, get it into the fridge within the two hours. Spread it in a shallow container so it cools fast. Then, eat it within about 3 to 4 days, and reheat it until it's steaming hot all the way through. If it's been out longer than two hours, bin it. It's not worth the risk, especially for kids, older people or anyone pregnant.

Alex: Cool it fast: split it into small shallow portions, or freeze single servings. Reheat only once, and skip leaving it warming on the stove. That's another spot where it can sit in the danger zone.

replies: Sam: No, don't give it ibuprofen. It's one of the more dangerous human painkillers for dogs, even in small doses. Downsides: it can cause stomach ulcers and bleeding, and it can damage the kidneys. Some dogs get sick from a single dose, and smaller dogs are at higher risk. Signs of trouble are vomiting, black stools, not eating, being unusually tired, or drinking and peeing a lot. If your dog has already had some, call a vet or a pet poison line right away. Don't wait for symptoms. Upside: there are dog-safe pain medicines. A vet can prescribe the right one for the dog's size and the cause of the pain. Next step: ring your vet today, describe the pain, and ask what's safe to give in the meantime. Same goes for paracetamol and aspirin, since they're not safe to guess with either. ! asked.ask: How many days are cooked leftovers good for in the fridge?
replies: Sam: Three to four days is the standard answer for cooked leftovers in a fridge set at 40°F (4°C) or colder. That covers most things: meat, rice, pasta, veggies, soups and casseroles. First, the clock starts when the food finishes cooking. It's best to get it into the fridge within two hours of that, or one hour if the room is hot. Then, store it in shallow, covered containers so it cools fast. After that, if you won't eat it by day four, freeze it. Frozen leftovers stay good for months. One warning: don't trust a sniff test. Bacteria that cause food poisoning often don't change the smell or look. Reheat leftovers until they're steaming hot, and toss anything you're unsure about. ! Careful: Don't trust a sniff test. asked.ask: How long can I keep last night's cooked dinner in the fridge?
replies: Sam: Three to four days is the safe limit for most cooked dinners, as long as they went into the fridge within two hours of cooking. So last night's meal is fine until about Monday at the latest. Downsides: smell and looks aren't a reliable test, since the bacteria that make you ill often don't change either. Rice and pasta are the ones to be careful with, so I'd eat those within a day or two. To keep it safe, put it in a shallow, covered container and keep the fridge at 5°C (41°F) or below. When you reheat it, get it steaming hot all the way through, and only reheat it once. If it's been sitting out for more than two hours, bin it. ! asked.ask: What is the boiling point of water in Fahrenheit?
replies: Sam: 212°F at sea level. That's 100°C. One thing to know: the boiling point drops as you go higher up. In the mountains, water boils at a lower temperature, so food like pasta or eggs can take a bit longer to cook. The higher you go, the lower the boiling point drops. Robin: Just check the water first: that 212°F only holds at sea level, so it's cooler up high. If you're purifying drinking water in the mountains, let it boil longer to be safe. Sam's pasta point is the small one.

asked.ask: At what temperature in °F does water boil?
replies: Sam: Water boils at 212°F at sea level. Higher up, where the air pressure is lower, it boils a bit cooler. In Denver, for example, it's around 202°F.

Robin: Just check the pot: steam and boiling water cause serious burns, so keep your face and hands back. Also, the boiling point drops roughly 1°F for every 500 ft you go up, which fits Sam's Denver number.
Alex: Heads up for Denver cooking: pasta and eggs take longer in cooler boiling water, so add a few minutes. Beans or tough cuts? A pressure cooker skips the problem.
